node-1.label: Bilateral conjunctival erythema and asymptomatic skin lesions on the lower limbs, trunk, and upper limbs

node-2.label: 65-year-old man with medical history of coronary artery disease, treated dyslipidemia, and hypertension; initial ophthalmology presentation showed bilateral conjunctival erythema and choroidal thickening

node-3.label: One year after initial presentation, asymptomatic skin lesions appeared on lower limbs and progressed to trunk and upper limbs; a 3-week tapered course of oral prednisone (60 mg/d) showed no improvement; physical examination revealed many flat, firm, brownish papules and plaques resembling keloids, some linear with an arborizing pattern, symmetrically involving lower limbs, trunk, and upper limbs while sparing face, oral mucosa, and flexor regions

node-4.label: One year later, immunoglobulin G–κ type monoclonal gammopathy developed

why.why: Pathologist analysis now explicitly favors NXG over scleromyxedema: the deep fibrosis with CD68+ histiocytes, Touton-like giant cells, hemosiderin deposition, absent mucin, low complement, and IgG-κ monoclonal gammopathy are more consistent with a histiocytic disorder. H&E lacking mucin directly weakens mucinosis, and positive mucin staining remains unconfirmed because special stains are missing. Thus scleromyxedema is less likely, lowered from 0.60 to 0.40.

New expert analyses report a normal bone marrow examination and negative Bence Jones protein, which further reduce the likelihood of systemic amyloidosis. The biopsy also shows a fibrosing histiocytic process without amyloid-type features. Together with the absence of classic amyloid skin features, these findings make systemic amyloidosis very unlikely, lowering confidence from 0.05 to 0.02.

New expert analyses report a normal bone marrow examination and negative Bence Jones protein, providing no evidence for a lymphoproliferative disorder. The biopsy shows a granulomatous fibrosing histiocytic infiltrate rather than lymphoid infiltration. These findings reduce the already low confidence in lymphoproliferative disorder from 0.03 to 0.02.
